Let d_j=s_j−s_+, p_j=softmax(βs)_j, w_j=(1−α)/K+αp_j. For weighted BPR L=Σ stopgrad(w_j)softplus(d_j), ∂L/∂s_j=w_j sigmoid(d_j), and ∂L/∂s_+=−Σw_j sigmoid(d_j). This is uniform-smoothed self-adversarial weighting; [RotatE’s implementation](https://github.com/DeepGraphLearning/KnowledgeGraphEmbedding/blob/master/codes/model.py) likewise detaches softmax weights, but applies pointwise logistic losses. Without detachment, each negative gradient additionally contains αβp_j(ℓ_j−Σp_kℓ_k). Detachment therefore changes the update, beyond its numerical weighting.

[BPR-max](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf) instead uses L=−log A, A=Σp_jq_j, q_j=sigmoid(s_+−s_j): logarithm outside the weighted probability sum, versus weighted negative log-probabilities. With its original β=1 and differentiated weights, ∂L/∂s_j=p_j−p_jq_j²/A; this differs from detached weighted BPR. [PSL, NeurIPS 2024](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/db1d5c63576587fc1d40d33a75190c71-Paper-Conference.pdf), uses log Σa(d_j)^(1/τ), yielding gradient a′(d_j)a(d_j)^(1/τ−1)/(τΣa(d_k)^(1/τ)). Its shifted tanh/atan/ReLU activations reshape gradient influence; uniform mixing does not inherit PSL’s analysis.

Algebraically, duplicate negatives accumulate: an item appearing m times receives total weight m(1−α)/K+αm exp(βs)/(Σcolumns exp(βs_k)). Thus column bounds (1−α)/K≤w_j≤α+(1−α)/K do not provide the same bound per unique item. Duplicates also change BPR-max and PSL sums through multiplicity. Such bounds limit individual score-gradient contributions for logistic BPR, but do not establish false-negative robustness: hard false negatives can still dominate collectively, and parameter gradients additionally depend on score Jacobians. Deduplication or multiplicity correction addresses repeated-item concentration; noise robustness requires additional assumptions or measured evidence.
